h: The Soul of Torah and the Gift of Light

p: Now, in the zemiros of the holy Arizal,
we ask for the revelation of secrets,
as in "May He send us…" and so on,
"and we shall see…" and so on,
"and may He show us His hidden things";
and further on, "May He reveal to us the reasons…" and so on,
"Rejoice, harvesters of the field…" and so on,
with a precious secret," and so on.
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג קנב, א)
In the holy Zohar on this parshah (Zohar III 152a):
that the Torah came to present
and the talk of common folk…" and so on.
and the words of the Torah,
which are called 'the bodies of Torah'…" and so on,
which are the stories of this world…" and so on.
do not look at the garment
but at the body…" and so on.
"The wise ones, servants of the supernal King,
those who stood at Mount Sinai,
which is the root of everything,
And in the World to Come
at the soul of the soul of the Torah."
that whoever does not know the secrets of the Torah
did not stand at Mount Sinai.
the Chida, of blessed memory, wrote:
Rather, it means one who does not believe
in the secrets of the Torah," and so on.
do not look at the garment
but at the body, and so on,
and those who stood at Mount Sinai
look only at the soul, and so on.
So it is explicit that it speaks of contemplation:
that these contemplate only the bodies of Torah,
while those who stood at Mount Sinai
which is the root of everything,
just as the gloss mentioned above explained.
And in truth it is astonishing to say so,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַב חִידָ״א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
as the Chida, of blessed memory, wrote above.
as meaning the secrets of the Torah.
in the holy Zohar cited above:
"And in the World to Come they are destined to look
at the soul of the soul."
Now if that refers to secrets,
that only in the World to Come
"are they destined to look," and so on?
Were not the secrets of the Torah revealed
So of necessity the meaning is
and that belongs only to the World to Come,
while "the soul" means the secrets of the Torah
that were revealed to the masters of Kabbalah
And from this they drew the implication
that whoever does not grasp the secrets,
did not stand at Mount Sinai;
and that is difficult, as said above.
there are the bodies of Torah,
how one is to conduct oneself;
in garments, which are stories," and so on;
lessons in the ways of the world,
What is the point of Timna?
She was a daughter of kings," and so on;
Because they should not have pushed her away."
that the Avos ought not to have pushed her away,
her intention was not for the sake of Heaven;
for had her intention been for the sake of Heaven,
מוּטָב שֶׁתְּהֵא שִׁפְחָה לְאוּמָּה זוֹ וְכוּלֵּי
"better to be a maidservant to this nation," and so on,
Amalek would not have come forth from her;
רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הַמְכֻוָּון שֶׁלָּהּ
it was only because her aim
was not, at its depth, for the sake of Heaven.
and this is called the bodies of Torah.
From this even the nations are not excluded;
for the pious of the nations of the world too,
the seven mitzvos of the children of Noach,
are counted among the pious of the nations of the world,
that the holy Zohar cited above speaks of
"The soul of man is the lamp of Hashem";
that is, the light from the Torah
that shines in the heart of Yisrael,
הוּא רַק לְאִינּוּן דְּקַיְימָא בְּטוּרָא דְּסִינַי
belongs only to "those who stood at Mount Sinai,"
שֶׁכָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת עָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי
for all the souls stood at Mount Sinai,
דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינּוּן לָא הֲווֹ
for even though they themselves were not there,
Since he will be called by the name Yisrael,
כְּבָר הָיְתָה נִשְׁמָתוֹ עַל הַר סִינַי
his soul was already at Mount Sinai.
And as for what we find in the Gemara (Nedarim 20a),
"It is known that his forefathers did not stand
that refers to the standing of the forefathers,
who stood bodily at Mount Sinai;
this one's forefathers did not stand there.
and those who are not here";
And here, where the holy Zohar mentions
even the souls of the converts.
And this is what it says:
"The wise ones, servants of the King,
which is the root of everything,
that is in the bodies of the Torah,
in the heart of every one of Yisrael
when he turns himself to it.
וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And this is the aspect of the light of Torah she'b'al peh:
that the words of Torah enter
that there is an aspect of Torah she'b'al peh
even in a pasuk of the Torah
into the depths of the heart.
And this is called the mysteries
"The secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him";
is a secret for those who fear Him,
"Her husband is known in the gates,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (וַיֵּרָא, חֵלֶק א קג, ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (Vayera, Zohar I 103b).
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תִשָּׂא לד)
And about this Chazal said (Tanchuma Ki Sisa 34),
"Were I to write for him the multitude of My Torah,
they would be counted as something alien," and so on:
The Mishnah, which was given orally," and so on.
And this is the Torah she'b'al peh:
when the words of Torah enter the heart
And to this only Yisrael can attain,
and the nations of the world are excluded from it,
which is a drawing forth of wisdom,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (יִתְרוֹ, חֵלֶק ב פ, א)
as is written in the holy Zohar (Yisro, Zohar II 80a).
His statutes and His judgments to Yisrael":
for a Jew grasps light in the heart
לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי (שָׁם, כ)
"He has not done so for any nation" (Tehillim 147:20):
the statutes they do not accept,
"and the judgments, they do not know them";
for even what the nations of the world practice
which obligates them because it is fitting,
such as honoring father and mother
for one does not bring da'as into them.
As the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote
that one who accepts the seven mitzvos,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
of whom Chazal said that he has a share in the World to Come
and is among the pious of the nations of the world,
is so only when he accepts them and performs them
that the children of Noach had already been commanded in them;
he is not a ger toshav
nor one of the pious of the nations of the world, and so on.
And this is "the judgments, they do not know them."
And this is what the holy Zohar says,
that "the wise ones, servants of the supernal King,
those who stood at Mount Sinai,
that is, at the light of Torah
that is in the bodies of Torah,
which are the halachos and a person's conduct;
and this light that enters the heart
every one of Yisrael can attain;
when he turns himself to the words of Torah,
he grasps the light within the words of Torah,

and seven pipes to the lamps,

from the olive trees to the bowl and to the lamps.

the main spread of Torah she'b'al peh,
through the Men of the Great Assembly,

were a hundred and twenty elders,

and what was his name? Nechemiah," and so on.
the spread of Torah she'b'al peh,
and the principal figure was Zerubavel,
and concerning Torah she'b'al peh it is stated
that it comes with great toil
and the overturning of the mountain like a tub
הָיָה רַק עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
was only on account of Torah she'b'al peh;
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which is the aspect of the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
for the olive trees pour out the oil of themselves,
"which pour the golden oil out of themselves…"
And although a person must toil
nevertheless after all the toil and effort,
the essential bestowal of Torah she'b'al peh
"It is vain for you who rise up early…
who eat the bread of toil";
they obtain the bread of Torah
"so He gives to His beloved in sleep."
For Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
to him was given all the lower wisdom,
as a gift, in one night,
זֶה דְּבַר ה׳ אֶל זְרוּבָּבֶל לֵאמוֹר
"This is the word of Hashem to Zerubavel, saying:
And this corresponds to the holiness
for the Avos, Avraham and Yitzchak,
comes only from Hashem Yisbarach alone,
"I am speaking of those rich in Torah," and so on;
as referring to the wise and the foolish.
strength is the name for fear of Hashem Yisbarach,
"not by might," which is words of Torah,
"and not by strength," which is fear of Heaven,
that comes through a person's own effort;
כִּי אִם בְּרוּחִי אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
"but by My spirit, says Hashem of Hosts":
which Hashem Yisbarach bestows of His own accord
and My words that I have placed in your mouth."
"The king is not saved by a great army."
for the Sages are called kings (Gittin 62a):
he is not saved through words of Torah alone.
וְזֶה כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
שֶׁשָּׁם הִשְׁווּ כָּל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי
for there all the nations of the world agreed," and so on;
You are king over us," and so on.
"A mighty man is not rescued by great strength":
the mighty one who conquers his yetzer
is not rescued by great strength,
that is, by fear and dread
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
And this alone does not avail either,
and "whoever is greater than his fellow,
his yetzer is greater than he,"
"The horse is a false hope for salvation" (Tehillim 33:17):
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צו, א)
in the manner of what Chazal said (Sanhedrin 96a):
who ran before Me like horses";
so effort is likened to a horse.
is also "a false hope for salvation."
"Nor will it deliver by its great might":
for the words of Torah too
הִנֵּה עֵין ה׳ אֶל יְרֵאָיו (שָׁם, יח)
"Behold, the eye of Hashem is upon those who fear Him (Tehillim 33:18),
upon those who hope for His kindness";
who recognize that everything is from the kindnesses of Hashem.
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
And this is what He said (Chullin 89a):
for that counted as nothing to Avraham;
rather, it refers to the greatness
that he attained in the light of Torah
which in his eyes was elevation and greatness;
for he did not attribute this
to his own strength and effort alone.
that this was not from his own effort
but only from the salvation of Hashem Yisbarach.
And upon them is the eye of Hashem, to help them,
"And were it not…" and so on;
ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ (תְּהִלִּים לז, לג)
"Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" (Tehillim 37:33).
וְזֶהוּ לְהַצִּיל מִמָּוֶת נַפְשָׁם (שָׁם לג, יט)
And this is "to rescue their soul from death" (Tehillim 33:19):
"a mighty man is not rescued by great strength,"
which is the rescue from the yetzer hara;
"And to keep them alive in famine":
that is, in words of Torah,
bestows words of Torah upon them.
And the Avos, Avraham and Yitzchak,
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach
and in truth Avraham and Yitzchak too
nevertheless at the time of the effort
and therefore from Avraham came forth refuse,
and likewise from Yitzchak came forth refuse,
for even at the time of effort
לֵית אֲנָא מוֹבִיד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי
"I will not give up my hope in my Creator"
This is why his bed was complete,
and such a one merits the true light
so that it will not cease even from his descendants.

p: And this is what is said in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30):
"'Let there be light' (Bereishis 1:3) is the right;
'and there was light' is the left,
is an expression of pain," and so on;
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
"'And God saw the light, that it was good' (Bereishis 1:4)
which is good," and so on.
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach;
only with Avraham, refuse remained among his offspring.
"'Let there be light': this is Avraham"
that the refuse is not his offspring.
"And there was light" corresponds to Yitzchak,
and in him the light already had established existence,
for he was already called Yisrael,
who was circumcised at eight days;
only, it was in his power
to uproot the name Yisrael from himself.
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
"And God saw the light, that it was good":
in whom the light remained forever,
since his bed was already complete;
and no Jew whatsoever is able
even if his sins grow great, Heaven forbid;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
"even though he sinned, he is a Yisrael"
And so it is expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (2:3):
וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ה)
which is "the word of Hashem to Zerubavel";
for at that time, when there began
the spread of the Torah she'b'al peh
they should not attribute it to a person's effort;
which is the power of words of Torah,
"and not by strength," which is fear of Heaven,
and these are the attributes of Avraham and Yitzchak;
that is, that they should recognize
that everything comes from Hashem Yisbarach,
the light of Torah she'b'al peh:
"so He gives to His beloved in sleep,"
when the Daughter is crowned with the Avos,
all the holiness of the three Avos,
the light of Torah she'b'al peh
for the holiness of this Shabbos
is the matter of lighting the Menorah,
